From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sam Trench <sam.trench@aurora-cloud.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Aurora: remediation credit authorization & customer remediation plan

Team —

Following the multi-region latency spikes on 2027-04-12 (incident INC-20270412-1276) Aurora experienced elevated P95 tail latency for ~3.5 hours during their peak traffic window. Customer impact: increased request timeouts for their public-facing search product and multiple internal escalations to their SREs.

Customer ask: an operational remediation package + financial concession while we finalize the KV-cache change and kernel fix (ETA next week). They specifically asked for: 
- a bill credit to cover the incident window and customer goodwill, and
- a capacity credit for one month to offset reload/retune costs.

Proposal (commercial):
- One-time remediation credit: $60,000 (applied to their May invoice)
- Capacity credit: 2 months of their committed Dedicated pool (equivalent to ~$18,500/month)
- Add 90-day overage protection at 50% discount

Rationale: keeps renewal on track (Aurora is in active negotiations for an enterprise renewal; current ARR ~ $1.2M), limited precedent (we've done similar but typically capped at $50k). I attached a short incident summary and the proposed credit calculation.

Request: need exec sign-off for anything > $50k. Can we get a decision today so I can communicate to Sam and Priya?

Attachments: incident_summary_20270412.pdf, aurora_usage_q1.csv, proposed_credit_calc.xlsx

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Director, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Mobile: (415) 555-0182

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora: remediation credit authorization & customer remediation plan

Marissa —

Thanks for the write-up and the attach. A couple quick notes:
- The math in proposed_credit_calc.xlsx looks right to me for direct MRR impact, but we should include the retention upside if we expect them to exercise renewal option this summer.
- Customer sentiment is fragile; Sam explicitly said they want "meaningful" compensation to avoid procurement escalation.

Recommendation: increase the one-time credit to $75k (we can frame it as $60k incident + $15k goodwill) OR keep $60k but add a renewal credit (10% on first-year renewal). The $75k path is cleaner and reduces negotiation noise.

If we're ok with $75k I can approve internally for up to $80k on margin grounds; will need legal to sign off on the language if we add a renewal concession.

-rishi

Marissa / Rishi —

From CS and the AM check-ins: Aurora is at high risk of pushing this past procurement unless they see an immediate substantive offer. They escalated to their Head of Platform (Priya) and asked for written assurances.

I support the $75k ask if we're comfortable with the precedent. Two small asks to operationalize:
- Add a short SOW amendment language that ties the credit to the close of the incident (no double-dipping) and requires Aurora to sign an acceptance of the remediation plan.
- Include a postmortem delivery commitment: full RCA + timeline for the KV-cache fix (we already committed to next-week patch).

I believe the total economic hit (if we go $75k + 2 months capacity credit at ~$37k) is manageable vs. losing the deal.

Legal review / quick notes:
- We can approve a one-time credit up to $100k without requiring Board notification, provided there's no change to the existing SLA terms.
- If we attach any renewal/discount language, that constitutes a commercial amendment and requires the customer to sign an addendum (we should avoid open-ended commitments).
- Recommend including a one-paragraph release clause: "This one-time remediation credit resolves claims arising from the incident detailed in INC-20270412-1276 and does not alter the SLA in place." Keeps precedent clean.

If you want us to draft the short addendum and release, we can turn it around by EOD.

-Lauren
